summary: Iter63 tested shift address/Get directions, overdue invoice alerts (API, digest function, UI banner and pills) and Email to payer (API, shared PDF link, UI sheet and toast). Backend: 18/18 pytest pass once the payer email is delivered@resend.dev. The Emergent email service blocks @example.com recipients (422 undeliverable_recipient), so the app returns 502. The public ingress replaces that 502 JSON body with an HTML page, so the UI only shows 'Something went wrong'. Frontend: all requested flows work at 390x844. Directions open https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=1%20Hay%20Street%2C%20Perth%20WA%206000, and tapping the button does not also open the card's detail sheet. Deprecated packages detected: none in the files reviewed.

minor.issue: If the email fails, the route raises HTTPException(502). Through the public ingress, a 502 response body is replaced with an HTML page (<!DOCTYPE html>), so the JSON detail 'The email couldn't be sent...' never reaches the app. The frontend api() falls back to 'Something went wrong'. Verified: localhost:8001 returns the JSON detail, but the public URL returns HTML.

Every email failure is reported as 'Try again in a minute', even a permanent one. The service returns 422 'Undeliverable recipient' for bad addresses and 429 rate_limited (seen in logs). Retrying will never fix a bad address; that case should say the payer email looks invalid.

The invoice_links token is inserted before send_email. Each failed attempt leaves an orphan link that still opens the PDF for 60 days. Insert the link only after a successful send, or delete it on failure.
The meta key for the day is inserted before send_overdue_digest runs. If the digest throws halfway, for example during the email loop, no retry happens that day. Low risk.

ui_bugs.issue: When the email service fails, the toast shows the generic 'Something went wrong' (caused by the ingress 502 replacement above).

issues: The Overdue pill uses the same 'accent' tone as Unpaid, so overdue invoices only differ by label. Use an error/warning tone.
'Email to payer' still shows when the payer has no email (TEST63-008). Tapping it returns a 400 with a helpful message, but disabling or hiding it with a hint would be clearer.
The 'Emailed to ... · DD-MM-YYYY' date comes from UTC emailed.at.slice(0,10), so it can show the previous day for emails sent before 8am Perth.
'Get directions' still shows on awaiting_approval shifts that the worker has already clocked out of (shf_ui63c). Consider also hiding it for awaiting_approval.

action_items: Change the email-failure status in POST /api/invoices/{id}/email from 502 to one the ingress passes through (e.g. 503 if verified, or 424/422/400), so the UI shows the real message.
Map the email service's 422 undeliverable_recipient to a clear 'payer email looks invalid' message. Keep 'try again' for 429 and 5xx. This needs send_email to return the reason or status.
Create the invoice_links token only after a successful send, or delete it on failure.
Optional UX: a distinct tone for the Overdue pill; disable 'Email to payer' when the payer has no email; hide directions for awaiting_approval shifts; show the emailed date in Perth time.
critical_code_review_comments: send_overdue_digest only emails and notifies non-hidden admin/finance users. In this environment that means the four real executives (andrewt@, pronathin@, rond@, justined@nolimitts.com.au). Any TEST invoices in the DB after 8am Perth would be emailed to them. The tests guard this by pre-inserting the day's meta key and by monkeypatching send_email and notify.
Hidden test admins (user_testadmin01/02) never get the digest, so the real notification path can't be checked end to end with the test accounts.
Exact clock-in lat/lng is correctly stripped for non-office users in both /shifts and /shifts/{id}.

success_rate.backend: 100% (18/18; the email send passes only with delivered@resend.dev, @example.com is rejected by the email service with 502)
success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all flows work; the error toast message is degraded)

It also adds a guard meta key, overdue_invoices_<today> with test_guard=iter63. 'clean' removes all of it by id, including invoice_links. context_for_next_testing_agent: Use delivered@resend.dev as the payer email for successful sends; @example.com gets 422 from the Emergent email service. Run pytest with -n 0. The test uses a module-level event loop for direct motor access. Perth 'today' in this environment is 2026-11-06. Seed before the tests and clean after: python tests/ui_seed_iter63.py seed|clean.
rca_of_issue: Generic 'Something went wrong' on email failure: send_email returned False (422 undeliverable for example.com), so the route raised HTTPException(502). The k8s ingress swaps upstream 502 bodies for its own HTML page. api.ts JSON-parses the body, finds no detail and falls back to the generic text. Repro: POST <public>/api/invoices/{id}/email for a payer @example.com returns 502 with an HTML body, while the same call on localhost:8001 returns 502 {"detail":"The email couldn't be sent..."}. Fix: return a non-502 status.
